On Al Jazeera.

Dozens have died in the central Philippines in the wake of Typhoon Kalmaegi #TinoPH. The storm barreled through a region still reeling from a major earthquake, and triggered widespread flooding that forced residents to their roofs and displaced hundreds of thousands. Local officials say a number of people remain missing.

quoted_tweet.text: Disaster has struck Cebu in the Philippines, specifically in and around Cebu City. The passage of Typhoon Kalmaegi (TinoPH) over the last 24 hours has unleashed ~2 FT of rainfall over the island, sparking massive, urban flash floods that have claimed 48+ lives and left many more missing. Early reports indicate that at least 200,000 homes in Cebu City have either been inundated or destroyed.

Now making landfall across the Mimaropa region of the Philippines with renewed convection, Typhoon Kalmaegi (TinoPH) is already setting his sights on re-intensifying to Category 2 strength after ravaging the island of Cebu with flooding. His next landfall, slated for southern Vietnam, may take place roughly ~48 hours from now, during which time Kalmaegi will try to reach a 110 mph (175 kph) secondary peak over the South China Sea. The last Category 2+ storm to make landfall south of the city of Da Nang was Noru in 2022. 

Prepare now if you’re in Kalmaegi’s path.
